Eder (town)
EE-der
proper noun
Hebrew Eder, “flock” or “fold”; a town in the far south of Judah toward the border of Edom, named once; distinct from the tower of Edar near Bethlehem.

Biblical Definition

Eder was a town among the uttermost cities of Judah toward the coast of Edom, listed at the head of that southern roll: “And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward were Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur” (Josh 15:21). The name means “flock” or “fold,” fitting for a town in the great grazing lands of the south, where flocks and herds were the wealth of the people. This town is distinct from the tower of Edar near Bethlehem where Jacob spread his tent. A fold on the frontier is a homely and fitting picture of the people of God, who are His flock, the sheep of His pasture. The LORD is the Shepherd of Israel, who leads Joseph like a flock; and the Lord Jesus is the good Shepherd who gives His life for the sheep and gathers them into one fold. Eder, a sheepfold-town on the edge of the wilderness, preaches the tender care of the Shepherd who seeks the straying, binds up the broken, and will bring all His scattered flock at last into the fold where there shall be one flock and one Shepherd.

Webster 1828 Definition

A town in the far south of Judah toward Edom, “flock” or “fold” (Josh 15:21); a picture of the people of God as His flock, and of the good Shepherd who gathers them.

Modern Corruption

A sheepfold-town of the far south; it recovers the picture of God’s people as His flock and of the good Shepherd who gathers and keeps them.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A town named once at the edge of the desert draws no modern quarrel. Its homely name, “fold,” simply turns the mind to the flock of God and the Shepherd who keeps it. This town is a distinct place from the tower of Edar near Bethlehem.

The principle to recover is that the people of God are His flock. The LORD is the Shepherd of Israel; the Lord Jesus is the good Shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep and knows His own by name. A fold on the southern frontier preaches His tender care: He seeks the straying, carries the lambs in His bosom, and will gather all His scattered sheep into one fold under one Shepherd.
